description: Request-side contracts every case invoke/query action must meet before it reaches the product (step2r round 12, run-driven: docs/execution/s5a-adapter/run-61bd0f8a.json showed every api command and most queries rejected for envelope shape). verification/cases/request_contract.py applies and checks them; ./verify prepare runs verification/cases/check_request_contracts.py (PreparationAssetChecks 'request-contracts'), so a violation fails preparation and a recorded product gap prints KNOWN_OPEN. Step 2 round 13 replaces grantComposition with grantAuthorization: one all-of grant per actor, checked statically against every authorized read and command and every pinned FORBIDDEN. Product code is read, never changed.

commandRoutes.provenanceRule: provenance names every slot exactly once. A value whose provenance the case states (formerly embedded in the slot value or a per-slot valueProvenance map) keeps it. Otherwise a value the requester picked from the fixture world or an earlier response ($alias, $result, $transform, typed {type,id} or a list of only those) is CONTEXT, and a literal the requester typed in the request (text, decimal, boolean, quantity, aggregate) is USER. APPROVED_DEFAULT is never inferred; only a case statement sets it. A blanket valueProvenance string is not a per-slot statement and is ignored.

notChecked.blob: evidence download surface, no product query endpoint (adapter NOT_IMPLEMENTED)

queryEnvelope.operationsWithoutProductHandler: an operation outside 'operations' has no product handler at ce4970c4; only the shared envelope is checked and any parameter outside it needs a knownOpen entry
queryEnvelope.requiresNote: requires lists the identifiers of which a read names at least one (InventoryQueries object/inventory/trace, WorkReadHandler, DefinitionQueries, PolicyQueries, IdentityQueries getGrant); without them the product answers TYPE_INVALID before any authorization or business rule.
queryEnvelope.objectTypesNote: Noun types getObject/searchObjects serve (ApplicationQueries base types plus every ObjectReadProvider.objectTypes at ce4970c4). The type travels as scope.objectType: a top-level type lifts into filters, which provider handlers such as RegulatoryQueries refuse.
queryEnvelope.dedicatedReadsNote: A getObject of a non-noun target reads it through the plan's own read (plan section 3.4: Work through getWork, definitions through getDefinition; product PolicyQueries, IdentityQueries getGrant, EvidenceQueries getReconciliation).

harnessDeclarations.description: Values a case needs that are not product request content move to the action's 'harness' object (contracts/acceptance-case.schema.json); adapters read them and never send them as request fields.
harnessDeclarations.testBarrier: testTransactionId/testParticipantId/testBarrierId/testBarrierPoint of a racing call (the same values as its barrier control parameters)
harnessDeclarations.environmentId: the runtime environment a call or read targets (restore and archive cases)
harnessDeclarations.authenticationTest: credential variant the adapter signs (T08 issuer/subject/audience)
harnessDeclarations.executionContext: worker-route runtime task context (V7); the product binds it from the scheduled task, never from the payload
harnessDeclarations.mcp: MCP protocol fields outside tool arguments: transport rpcId, MRTR requestState and inputResponses (V6)
harnessDeclarations.intentionalViolation: a field the case sends on purpose to prove the product rejects it; prepare requires the declared fields to equal the actual violations and a pinned rejection on the action

grantAuthorization.rule: User decision 2026-10-09 (AGENTS.md): a grant naming several dimension kinds authorizes only when every kind matches the targets the product presents (all-of, IdentityAuthorization.permittedScopes); identifiers within one kind are alternatives, and the policy guard requires every presented identifier of a command (PolicyCommandGuard.everyScope). The fixture schema and the Step 3 installer hold one grant per actor, so a fixture grant keeps only the dimension kinds that every capability the cases call with that actor presents (directly or through it as a fixture delegator): ITEM when all those capabilities carry the item (familiesWithoutItem name those that do not), none otherwise (an organization-wide grant). WORK, PLACE, TARGET and SOURCE restrictions of a multi-purpose grant would refuse its own reads (an inventory or item row presents no WORK; a Work presents no PLACE), so conform_fixture drops them unless an override keeps them for a negative oracle. Keys with no product grant scope kind are dropped too: the installer could not install them. check_request_contracts.py then proves statically, per subcase, that every read or command the case expects to be authorized is covered and that every action pinned to FORBIDDEN stays uncovered.
productRefs: backend/src/main/java/com/mulino/application/identity/IdentityAuthorization.java (permittedScopes: membership, CapabilityAssignment, Grant with GrantAction, every non-ORGANIZATION grant scope kind present in targets with a matching id, delegator permitted for the same targets)
backend/src/main/java/com/mulino/application/policy/PolicyCommandGuard.java (everyScope: every single-id combination of the command scopes must pass)

verification/harness/src/main/java/org/mulino/verification/actual/ScenarioFixtureInstaller.java (grants: one grant per actor, scope kinds ITEM/WORK/PLACE/TARGET/SOURCE; workItem infers a Work item from grant scopes when the work entry names none)
grantAuthorization.unrepresentedNote: mulino_identity_GrantScopes.scopeKind is CHECKed to ORGANIZATION, TARGET, WORK, ITEM, PLACE, SOURCE; the installer drops these keys and reports the fixture incomplete. The grant is installed without them, so conform_fixture removes them instead of letting a fixture claim a restriction the product never enforces.

NULL.meaning: authorize(context, capability, null): any active grant with the capability passes (ApplicationQueries.java:55 for getAccessContext, IdentityQueries.java:15)

INVENTORY.meaning: every visible fixture segment of the item {TARGET:segment, ITEM:item, PLACE:segment place}; when none is visible the item row {TARGET:item, ITEM:item} must pass (InventoryQueries.java:87-88)

OBJECT.meaning: the requested row by noun type: TradeItem/ManufacturingLot {TARGET, ITEM}, QuantitySegment {TARGET, ITEM, PLACE}, Place {TARGET, PLACE}, Work {TARGET, WORK, ITEM}, PurchaseOrder/PurchaseProposal {ITEM, WORK}, Customer/Supplier {TARGET}; other provider nouns are not modelled (InventoryQueries.java:146-157, PurchaseQueries.java:20, SalesQueries.java:22)

WORK_ROW.meaning: the Work row {TARGET:work, WORK:work, ITEM:work item} (WorkReadHandler.java:65, WorkLifecycle.java:34)

ORGANIZATION.meaning: {ORGANIZATION:org} only: a grant naming any dimension fails (ItemCommands.java:33, PolicyCommands.java:20)

STOCK.meaning: each source leaf {TARGET:segment, ITEM:item, PLACE:segment place}, a move also {PLACE:destination}; the policy guard requires every value (InventoryCommands.java:45,64,82-84)

FULFILLMENT.meaning: {TARGET:segment, ITEM:item, PLACE:segment place (+transit place of a dispatch), WORK:sales line work} (FulfillmentCommands.java:28,31,38)

ITEM_TRADE.meaning: trade and evidence scopes that always carry the item of the row (purchase {ITEM, WORK, PLACE, SUPPLIER}, sales/receipt/delivery/return/recall {TARGET, ITEM, PLACE, WORK}, settlement {ITEM, WORK, PLACE, SUPPLIER|CUSTOMER}, shipment {ITEM, TARGET, PLACE, WORK}, regulatory {ITEM, TARGET, WORK, SOURCE}, evidence rows {TARGET, ITEM?, PLACE?, WORK?, SOURCE}); only the ITEM value is modelled

IDENTITY.meaning: the requested or stored grant/assignment scopes (IdentityCommands.java:19-22, IdentityControlGuard.java:17-66, IdentityQueries.java:20-26); not modelled, never assumed to carry ITEM

NO_HANDLER.meaning: no product handler is installed (contracts/request-contracts.json queryEnvelope operationsWithoutProductHandler, missing CommandHandler): the product answers VERSION_UNSUPPORTED before any authorization, so the grant decides nothing

GRANT_READ.meaning: the read grant's own GrantScopes plus TARGET:grant (IdentityQueries.java:20-26); a holder reading a grant of its own item scope presents that item. Values are not modelled

grantAuthorization.overridesNote: (fixtureId, actor) entries whose grant keeps named scope keys after conform_fixture, each with the negative oracle that needs the restriction. Empty unless a check shows a pinned FORBIDDEN that only a dimension restriction refuses.

decisionAuthority.meaning: Plan section 7.1 gives these actions a decision authority beyond the grant (MANAGER, QC, ADMIN, CONFIG_APPROVER, a guarded approval or ManagementAuthorities/ManagementCoverage of a HUMAN, backend PurchaseCommands.manager, RecallCommands.admin, ReturnCommands.manager, SettlementCommands.manager, ResponsibilityCommands.designated, IdentityControlGuard). A FORBIDDEN pinned on them is decided by that authority, so a grant that covers the call does not contradict it; the static check reports it as not judged instead of as a broken negative.

knownOpen.reason: contracts/intent.schema.json $defs.value has no array branch, yet the product handlers read list slots (InventoryCommands splitQuantity quantities and mergeQuantity segmentIds) and the plan's split/merge/multi-evidence commands need them. Cases keep their list slots; the product contract must publish an array value or an aggregate shape.
knownOpen.closeWhen: intent.schema.json allows the list representation the handlers read

knownOpen.reason: plan section 4.2 (line 122) defines action-specific eligible quantity; QueryRequests accepts top-level action/customerId but InventoryQueries rejects them as filters (Unsupported inventory filter).
knownOpen.closeWhen: getInventory answers eligibleQuantity for an action and customer

knownOpen.reason: cases read one obligation by id, the obligations of one kind or those of one allocation; getObligations takes only a work id and work filters. A read without a work id is refused (Work ID required).
knownOpen.closeWhen: the query contract names an obligation id/kind selector

knownOpen.reason: plan section 4.3 keys an inbox record by sourceNamespace+externalEventId+sourceVersion and links evidence to activities/occurrences; EvidenceQueries selects only by kind and a typed subject.
knownOpen.closeWhen: getInbox/getEvidence accept the source key, occurrence or activity selector

knownOpen.reason: an identity administrator reads another actor's access context (T08); getAccessContext answers only the caller.
knownOpen.closeWhen: the plan/product decide whether an administrator may read another actor's context

knownOpen.reason: plan section 4.2 traces a late-known defective subset of a mixed LOT; traceLot has no selector for the affected source.
knownOpen.closeWhen: traceLot or getTrace names the affected source

knownOpen.reason: T26 reads the Work a retried command touched by the command id; getWork takes only a work id.
knownOpen.closeWhen: the query contract names a command selector or the case reads the work id from the command result

knownOpen.reason: T19 reads the invoice-match assessment by invoice; getAssessment takes a work id only.
knownOpen.closeWhen: the query contract names an invoice assessment selector

knownOpen.reason: T02 searches two noun types at once; searchObjects takes one type.
knownOpen.closeWhen: searchObjects accepts several types or the case issues one search per type

knownOpen.reason: plan section 4.1 keeps ExternalIdentifier (issuer/namespace/validity) beside the internal id; T02 resolves an object by its issuer-scoped external identifier, which the object query has no selector for.
knownOpen.closeWhen: the object query names an external identifier selector

knownOpen.reason: T02, T07, T21 and V1 take the snapshot revision of an organization-wide observation (the observation names no item) from a read without an item or id; getInventory and getObject need one, so the plan's snapshotRevision has no organization-wide read.
knownOpen.closeWhen: the product offers an organization-scoped snapshot read, or the plan scopes these observations to an item

knownOpen.reason: T21 lists the organization's definitions (drafts included) after validation; getDefinition reads one pinned definition id.
knownOpen.closeWhen: the query contract names a definition listing

knownOpen.reason: C3 and V4 read each command target before the command to take its revision for expectedRevision (plan sections 4.2 and 7.3). These kinds have no product read: getObject serves only noun types and no dedicated read returns them.
knownOpen.closeWhen: a read returns the current revision of every command target kind
